name: Surf culture and surfwear
description: Beach-born style of surfers: boardshorts, rash vests, wetsuits, logo tees, caps and hoodies, built by the Australian Big Three (Billabong, Quiksilver, Rip Curl).

name: First Nations fashion (Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander)
description: Fashion and textile labels of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander designers and art centres: artist prints on resort wear, swimwear and gowns, celebrated by the National Indigenous Fashion Awards and Country to Couture.

name: Pasifika and Pacific Island fashion
description: Contemporary island wear of Polynesia, Melanesia and the Pacific diaspora: masi, tapa, bilum and elei motifs on puletasi, dresses, shirts and resort sets, shown at Fiji, PNG and Pacific Fusion fashion shows.

name: Robe mission (Mother Hubbard island dress)
description: Long, ample, brightly patterned missionary-era dress now worn as local costume across Polynesia and Melanesia (robe popinee, aelan dress, mu'umu'u, holoku), remade by Caledonian and Pacific dressmakers.

name: Bilum fashion (Papua New Guinea)
description: Dresses, outfits and garments woven in the Papua New Guinea bilum technique, begun as bilum dresses in 2002 and carried by designers at PNG Fashion Week.

name: Central Asian ethno-modern fashion
description: Urban, couture and ready-to-wear clothing from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan that rewrites nomadic and national dress (chapan, kamzol, felt, ornament, ikat) in modern cuts; shown at Visa Fashion Week Almaty and Tashkent and the Next Designer Award. Brands: Anima, Urpaq, Tamyr, Alkum Brand, Torem Ethnic, ZhSaken, NUR SHAH, Baira, Keshte, Chapansar.

name: Uzbek ikat and suzani fashion
description: Couture and ready-to-wear built on Margilan adras and ikat silks and Tashkent suzani embroidery, often cut as chapans, robes and quilted pieces; a revival backed by designers and artisan schools. Brands: Lali, Azukar Moreno, Dildora Kasimova, Bibi Hanum, Rano Collection, Human Wear, Suzani by Kasimbaeva, Mursak, Adras Republic.

name: Tbilisi post-Soviet underground fashion
description: Georgian fashion that draws on post-Soviet memory, club culture and punk rawness: collectives and labels shown at Mercedes-Benz Fashion Week Tbilisi, with the Vetements collective as the best-known export. Brands: Berhasm, Situationist, Krawaii, Tamra, Cosmic Dance.

name: Armenian heritage and taraz revival fashion
description: Yerevan labels that research and rework traditional Armenian costume, ornament, manuscripts and alphabet in modern clothing and festive dress, supported by Yerevan Fashion Week and the Fashion and Design Chamber. Brands: Shamshik, Teryan Cultural Center, Shabeeg, Shadoyan Fashion, Narny, Z.G.EST, Kivera Naynomis, Soghomonyan Fashion.

name: Sri Lankan batik and handloom fashion
description: Contemporary Sri Lankan labels built on batik, beeralu lace, handloom and the Kandyan osariya, shown at Colombo Fashion Week and Mercedes Benz Fashion Week Sri Lanka.

name: Newar and Dhaka dress revival (Nepal)
description: Revival and fusion of Nepali woven textiles and Newar dress, Haku Patasi, Dhaka, Chaubandi Cholo, as tailored coats, gowns and waistcoats.

name: Bhutanese contemporary kira and gho fashion
description: Bhutanese designers reworking the national dress, kira and gho, in handwoven textiles and new cuts, shown at Bhutan Fashion Week.

name: Khadi revival fashion (India)
description: Indian designers reinterpreting hand-spun, hand-woven khadi for contemporary wardrobes, such as the Navdhara Khadi showcase at Lakme Fashion Week.

name: Himalayan trekking and expedition wear (Nepal)
description: Mountain jackets, down layers, fleece and hand-knit caps made in Nepal for trekkers and climbers, sold in Thamel and Pokhara.

name: Pakistani lawn and unstitched seasonal fashion
description: Seasonal printed and embroidered lawn and khaddar sold unstitched or as pret by Pakistani houses such as Gul Ahmed, Khaadi, Sapphire and Alkaram.

name: Bengali festive wear (panjabi, fotua, sari)
description: Bangladeshi festive and ethnic clothing for Eid and Pohela Boishakh: panjabi, fotua, sari, salwar kameez and kurti, made with local handloom and block print.

name: Dhivehi libaas (Maldives)
description: Traditional Maldivian women's dress with kasabu gold-thread embroidery, worn at weddings and cultural events and revived by local designers.

name: Mexican streetwear
description: Mexico City, Guadalajara and Neza streetwear with its own graphics and references (skate and DIY roots, regional-Mexican, charro, paca and barrio culture): Pay's, Tony Delfino, Barragán, Headquarter México, Palida Studios, Thoro 650, MANCANDY, Diego Zúñiga.

name: Brazilian beachwear (moda praia)
description: Rio and Fortaleza bikini, maiô and saída-de-praia labels with Brazilian cuts and prints: Lenny Niemeyer, Salinas, Blueman, Cosmo Rio, SAU, Arya, Sage, Di Croce Al Mare.

name: Gaucho dress (bombachas de campo)
description: Argentine and Rioplatense country dress: bombachas de campo (baggy cotton trousers, Pampero brand), alpargatas, berets, belts and ponchos, sold by Gaucho Store and Gaucho Clothes.

name: Antillean madras dress (Wob Dwiyet, robe créole)
description: Creole women's dress of Dominica, Saint Lucia, Martinique and Guadeloupe: white chemise, lace petticoat, madras outer skirt and tête en l'air head tie, worn on Creole Day and for the quadrille; made by Blossom Dominica, Érudit, Madras & Cie and Kreoline Mode.

name: Andean alpaca knitwear
description: Peruvian alpaca sweaters, cardigans, ponchos and capes made from baby alpaca and suri: Kuna, Sol Alpaca, Incalpaca, Alpaca 111, Raffa, PAKA, Carla Quiroga (Bolivia), Amaru (Chile).

name: Cholita and pollera dress (Andes)
description: Aymara and Quechua women's pollera dress of La Paz and Cusco (wide gathered skirts, fringed shawls, bowler hats), taken into high fashion by Rosario Aguilar at Bolivia Moda and by Agustina in Cusco.

name: Mexican artisan-textile fashion
description: Contemporary Mexican labels built with Indigenous weavers, embroiderers and leatherworkers (Carla Fernández with 175 artisans, Amor & Rosas, Collectiva Concepción, Graziano & Gutiérrez).

name: Contemporary Indigenous fashion (First Nations, Inuit, Metis and Native American)
description: Designers and brands of Indigenous nations of North America who blend beadwork, ribbon work, regalia and nation-specific art with contemporary clothing; shown at Indigenous Fashion Weeks in Vancouver, Toronto and Santa Fe.

name: Cowichan sweater (Coast Salish hand-knit)
description: Heavy hand-knit sweater with sacred patterns knitted by Coast Salish artisans of Vancouver Island and mainland British Columbia from sheep wool; Indigenous makers contest machine-made imitations.

name: Baju Melayu and baju kurung (Malay national dress)
description: Malay dress of the baju Melayu for men and the baju kurung for women, national dress of Malaysia and Brunei, worn at Raya and formal occasions and reinterpreted by local labels.

name: Sinh and pha sin (Lao and Thai tube skirt revival)
description: Handwoven tube skirt of Laos and northern and north-eastern Thailand, worn daily in Laos and now recut by Thai and Lao labels into contemporary skirts and separates.

name: Songket, tenun and ikat woven-textile fashion
description: Contemporary clothing from hand-woven songket brocade, tenun and ikat cloth of Brunei, Malaysia and Indonesia.

name: Batik fashion
description: Clothing made from wax-resist dyed batik cloth, from Indonesian houses to Malaysian and Singaporean labels.

name: Modern Filipiniana (baro't saya and terno)
description: Philippine national women's dress of baro't saya and its descendants, reworked by contemporary designers in piña, jusi and local weaves.

name: Burmese longyi, htamein and inngyi
description: Myanmar national dress built on the longyi and htamein wrapped skirts with the inngyi top, modernised by Yangon boutiques.

name: Khmer sampot and krama
description: Cambodian wrapped sampot and the krama cloth, woven in silk and cotton and reworked in contemporary Cambodian fashion.

name: Habesha kemis (Ethiopian and Eritrean highland dress)
description: Long handwoven cotton dress with tilet or tibeb embroidery at hem, sleeves and neckline, worn with the netela shawl and mekenet sash; Shewa, Gojjam, Gondar and Wollo styles; Ethiopian Airlines crew uniform follows the zuria tilet form.

name: Herero dress (ohorokova)
description: Namibian Herero women's long Victorian-style dress with layered petticoats and the horned otjikaiva headdress, sewn by designers such as McBright Kavari for weddings and festivals.

name: Basotho blanket dress
description: Woollen blankets worn as clothing by Sotho people of Lesotho and South Africa, each design (Seana Marena, Lehlosi, Victoria England, Motlatsi, Moholobela) marking rank or life stage, with the mokorotlo straw hat.

name: Pantsula style
description: South African township dance subculture dressed in coordinated crews: Dickies work pants, bright collared shirts, Converse All Star sneakers and small-brim caps.

name: Izikhothane (skothane)
description: South African township showmanship culture of conspicuous consumption in loud, colourful designer apparel, layered and discarded to show wealth; began in Katlehong in the early 2000s.

name: Malagasy lamba and lambahoany
description: Madagascar's rectangular wrapped cloth worn by both sexes as sarong, bust-wrap, shoulder shawl or sash; the printed cotton lambahoany carries a proverb and is now the commonest form.

name: Maasai shuka
description: Red, blue or checked cotton cloth wrapped as the daily dress of Maasai people of Kenya and Tanzania, now reworked by Nairobi labels such as Wan Fam Clothing.

name: Akorino dress
description: White robes and turbans worn by members of the Akurinu (Holy Ghost Church of East Africa) in Kenya, whose scripture is said to require rejecting European dress.

name: Seshoeshoe (shweshwe) dress
description: Southern African printed dyed cotton (Three Cats by Da Gama Textiles) made up into dresses, skirts and wraps worn by married Sotho and Xhosa women and in contemporary South African fashion.

name: Post-Soviet streetwear (gopnik style)
description: Russian working-class and suburban gopnik dress of the 1990s taken to fashion weeks: graphic T-shirts with Cyrillic slogans, cropped jeans, loose sweatpants, sports socks, big-logo sportswear and Adilette slides.

name: Slavic chic (folk-craft revival fashion)
description: Polish and Ukrainian designers reviving embroidery, lace, crochet, hand-knitting and weaving from rural dress in luxury and slow fashion; the term Slavic Chic is credited to Magda Butrym.

name: Paninari (paninaro)
description: Milan-area Italian youth subculture of the 1980s defined by expensive designer labels (Stone Island, C.P. Company, Armani, Fila) mixed with American Timberland boots and Levi's jeans.

name: Nautical and marinière style (Breton stripe, sailor dress)
description: French navy-derived blue-and-white striped Breton shirt and related seafaring dress (pea coats, duffle coats, oilskins, sailor knits) worn as civilian fashion; made by Saint James, Armor Lux and Orcival and echoed by many houses.

name: Folk and fisherman knitwear (Aran, gansey, lopapeysa, Nordic patterned sweaters)
description: Hand- or machine-knitted wool sweaters of the North Atlantic fishing and farming regions: Irish Aran jumpers, Channel Island guernseys, Icelandic lopapeysur, Norwegian Setesdal and ski sweaters, Faroese star jumpers.

name: La Sape (Congolese sapeurs)
description: Dandy subculture of Kinshasa and Brazzaville (Societe des Ambianceurs et des Personnes Elegantes): designer suits, silk socks and bright colours, born of imitating European dress and revived at DRC Fashion Week 2026.

name: Lagos streetwear
description: Lagos skate- and music-linked streetwear labels (Severe Nature, Waffles n' Cream, Motherlan, Vivendii, wwyd, Pith) shown at the Street Souk market: tees, caps, hoodies, cargo trousers and denim with African prints.

name: Accra streetwear
description: Ghanaian streetwear labels of Accra and Tema (Free The Youth, Subwaestudios) making graphic tees, sweatshirts and denim that reimagine Ghanaian identity.

name: Abidjan streetwear
description: Abidjan labels (Djainin, Bana Bana, Mayeti, Toclo) sold in the Blu Lab African streetwear store: oversized denim jackets, screen prints and Japanese-inspired loose pants under a Nouchi street aesthetic.

name: Faso Dan Fani fashion
description: Clothing made from Burkina Faso's hand-woven cotton strip cloth, from Koro DK's AFRIK'In tees and polos to GX226 suits and dresses, promoted at Dan'Fani Fashion Week and Ouaga Fashion Week.

name: Bogolan fashion (Mali)
description: Couture and ready-to-wear built on Malian hand-dyed bogolan mud cloth by labels such as Haby Diallo, Gope Design, Anw Dambe and Farafina Tigne.

name: Abacost (Zairian suit)
description: Closed-front, tieless jacket suit introduced under Mobutu to replace the Western suit and revived by Kinshasa workshops such as Okasol.

name: Kaba and slit (Ghana)
description: Ghanaian women's ensemble of a fitted kaba blouse and a long slit skirt, now made up by couture houses such as Christie Brown, Pistis and Ajepomaa.

name: Adire and aso-oke fashion (Yoruba)
description: Nigerian labels working in Yoruba adire resist-dyed cloth and hand-woven aso-oke, from Maki Oh and Shop Ayora to Kenneth Ize and Deola Sagoe.

name: Raffia couture (Gabon and Congo)
description: Dresses, bustiers, skirts and ready-to-wear woven or trimmed in palm raffia by Chouchou Lazare in Libreville and Krechesse in Pointe-Noire.

name: Panu di terra fashion (Cabo Verde)
description: Clothing cut from Cabo Verde's hand-woven panu di terra cloth, from VAA Barros blazers and skirts to the ISLNDZ Olympic kit.

name: Kanvo fashion (Benin)
description: Garments in Benin's hand-woven kanvo cloth, produced by Loan-H in Cotonou and used for jackets by Rosyne Club.

name: New Chinese style and guochao
description: Domestic-brand pride and contemporary dress that reworks Chinese forms: mandarin collars, frog fastenings, qipao and mandarin jackets, mamian skirts and Tang-suit pieces in modern fabrics, from Shanghai designer labels to sportswear makers.

name: Taiwanese Urban Outdoor (functional urban fashion)
description: Taiwan-made technical fabrics in city clothes: water-repellent, wrinkle-resistant, multi-pocket, military- and outdoor-inspired menswear, led by WISDOM, GOOPiMADE, oqLiq and Guerrilla-Group.

name: Taiwanese vernacular-pop streetwear
description: Street clothes built on everyday Taiwan culture: betel-nut stands, temple colours, school notebooks, asparagus-juice cans and night-market kitsch, in high-saturation prints and loose silhouettes.

name: Hong Kong streetwear (CLOT and JUICE)
description: Hong Kong youth-culture streetwear launched in the 2000s around CLOT (2003) and the JUICE designer-streetwear store (2004), with Nike, Adidas and Converse collaborations.

name: Korean outdoor fashion
description: Korean mountain and trail brands worn as everyday fashion: shell jackets, down jackets, fleece, hiking trousers from Kolon Sport, Black Yak, Nepa, Millet Korea, CAYL and newer labels.

name: Mori kei (forest girl)
description: Loose, layered floaty dresses and cardigans in natural fabrics and neutral tones, with bangs and braids.

name: Fairy kei
description: Pastel dreamy 1980s-inspired look with bows, cardigans, tutus, over-the-knee socks and tea party shoes; name from the magazine Zipper.

name: Dolly kei
description: Vintage-style clothing inspired by Japan's view of the Middle Ages and European fairy tales, sometimes with religious symbols; associated with the Grimoire store.

name: Cult Party kei
description: Soft layered fabrics, cream lace, satin bows and Western religious motifs such as crosses and bibles, with natural makeup; named for the Harajuku shop Cult Party.

name: Jirai kei
description: Edgy dark-meets-kawaii look: blouses and frilly skirts with bows, hearts and crosses, black-white-dusky-pink palette, platform heels and chunky Mary Janes; with the softer ryosan-gata variant.

name: Genderless kei
description: Clothing that does not conform to gender norms, mostly worn by men.

name: Kogal
description: High-school uniform base with a shorter skirt, loose socks, often dyed hair, and a scarf.

name: Angura kei
description: Dark style blending Showa-era and traditional Japanese elements with goth touches, including kimono and modified school uniforms.

name: Oshare kei
description: Bright pop-style looks with heavy jewelry, anime-character bags, colourful hairclips and lighter makeup.

name: Heisei retro
description: Revival of 1990s and 2000s Japanese street fashion overlapping with Y2K and 1990s gyaru: loose socks, platform shoes, miniskirts, crop tops and loose street clothes, with Amekaji and Harajuku 2000s influences.

name: Contemporary gho and kira fashion (Bhutan)
description: Bhutanese designers reworking the national gho and kira and handloom textiles into modern collections, shown at the first Bhutan Fashion Week 2025 in Thimphu and Paro.

name: Timorese tais fashion (Timor-Leste)
description: Timorese designers turning hand-woven tais cloth into tailored jackets, dresses and accessories, working with women's weaving cooperatives.

name: Sudanese toub fashion (teyab designers)
description: Designer labels, many online, selling Sudanese toub (teyab) for casual, day, evening and wedding wear, in silk, chiffon and cotton, with painted and beaded variants.

name: Tajik atlas, adras and chakan fashion
description: Dushanbe designers working atlas and adras ikat silks and chakan embroidery into modern dresses and couture, shown at Tajikistan Fashion Week.

name: Saudi streetwear
description: Riyadh and Jeddah labels making hoodies, tees, cargos and bombers that mix urban wear with Saudi culture; 1886 is billed as the Kingdom's first streetwear brand and Riyadh Fashion Week shows it.

name: Palestinian heritage fashion (tatreez, Majdalawi, keffiyeh)
description: Contemporary Palestinian labels built on tatreez cross-stitch, Majdalawi weaving and the keffiyeh, from puffer-coat gowns to hoodies and abayas.

name: Algerian traditional couture (karakou, chedda, Kabyle dress, robe Naili)
description: Algerian couture houses whose specialties are the karakou, chedda, Kabyle dress, robe Naïli and blouza wahrania, shown as haute couture.

name: Tesettür (Turkish modest dress)
description: Turkish covered-dress fashion sold as its own category: tunics, ferace, pardesü, abayas, long coats, skirts and headscarves from chains and specialist labels.

name: Iranian manteau and rusari
description: Iranian women's everyday dress built on the manteau (long or short overcoat) and headscarf, with dozens of domestic brands dedicated to it.

name: Kurdish dress (şal û şapik, şemlek)
description: Kurdish men's şal û şapik ensemble and women's şemlek robe, qurte vest and coin headdress, now reworked by ateliers in Erbil and Sulaymaniyah.

name: Cairo streetwear
description: Local Egyptian labels selling hoodies, tees and cargos through Instagram and Cairo concept stores.

name: Tunisian streetwear
description: Tunisian streetwear labels that use clothing for social and political themes and local culture, working with local artists.

name: Capulana fashion (Mozambique)
description: Clothing, coats, shorts and turbans cut from capulana, the printed wrap cloth sold across Mozambique, by Maputo labels such as Chibaia, NT and Isis Mbaga; Mozambique no longer has its own textile industry, so cloth is printed elsewhere.

name: Chitenge fashion (Zambia)
description: Zambian designers cutting the printed chitenge cloth into bespoke tailoring, chitenge pants, blazers, mini-skirts and a reworked Lozi siziba, from labels such as Ensoko by Chiza, Lace by Mwenge and Nkanda Yatu.

name: UK roadman and grime dress
description: Black-dominated British street look of the 2000s grime and roadman scene: tracksuits, hoodies and oversized fits, puffer and hooded technical jackets, cargo-style trousers and Nike Air Max Plus trainers, worn partly as protection against CCTV; London labels such as Trapstar grew out of it.

name: Northeastern Brazilian authorial and artisanal fashion (Nordestesse)
description: Authorial labels from Bahia, Ceará, Alagoas and Paraíba that pair with local textile artisans and sell through the Nordestesse platform and its Mãos da Moda project: Catarina Mina, Marina Bitu, Foz, Dendezeiro, Santa Resistência, Inttuí, Teroy13, Areia da Bahia, Somos Dua, Carnavália, Morada, Sillas Filgueira, Gefferson Vila Nova.

name: Traje de flamenca (flamenco dress)
description: Andalusian festive women's dress of a fitted ankle-length frilled dress (polka dots the most popular), starched petticoats, Manila shawl and mantoncillo, worn at the Feria de Abril, romerías and flamenco shows; shown on runways at SIMOF by dedicated flamenco-fashion designers.

name: Traje de fallera (Valencian fallera dress)
description: Valencian festive women's dress of the Fallas, based on 18th and 19th century dress: jupón and enaguas, whalebone corpiño, lantern or French sleeves, pañuelo and delantal, in handwoven silk espolín brocade, made by specialist indumentaristas and silk mills.

name: Made in France textile and clothing (France Terre Textile)
description: Contemporary French clothing made inside France's five textile basins (Vosges, Alsace, Nord, Troyes-Champagne, Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes): knitwear, T-shirts, socks, underwear and jeans from small brands whose products are certified by the France Terre Textile label (over 75% of production steps in France) or similar origin labels; brands include Le Slip Francais, Garcon Francais, Lemahieu, 1083 and Maison Broussaud.

name: Basque coast and Landes surf-lifestyle labels
description: Independent surf-inspired clothing labels born in Hossegor, Guethary, Bidart and Biarritz as an alternative to the large listed surf brands, selling lifestyle collections such as Chipiron, Parlementia and Hopaal.

name: Zhongshan suit and Tang suit (Chinese heritage tailoring)
description: Chinese ceremonial and everyday menswear ranked as Zhongshan suits and Tang suits: old Beijing, Shanghai, Hangzhou and Ningbo tailoring houses (Hongdu, Longqingxiang, Refosian, Zhenxingxiang, Baromon, Rongchangxiang) beside newer labels (Mozen, Manloulan, Gege, Tao Yumei) and menswear groups such as Romon and Seven.

name: North-eastern Indian handloom and slow fashion
description: Labels from Meghalaya, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Tripura and Assam that build contemporary clothing on region-specific handlooms and weaves, such as Naga loin-loom textiles and Manipuri handlooms.

name: Indian handloom revival labels
description: Indian labels that revive and reframe traditional handloom weaving for contemporary wear, working with weavers and natural fibres.

name: Chikankari fashion (Lucknow)
description: Labels built on Lucknow chikankari hand embroidery, selling kurtas, sarees and ethnic sets worked by Lucknow artisans.

name: Celebrity-owned labels of Taiwan and Hong Kong (artist brands)
description: Clothing labels founded by singers, actors, radio hosts and TV personalities in the Taiwanese and Hong Kong pop scenes: tees, caps and street casuals sold on the founder's fame and collaborations (StayReal, Outer Space, SMG, M JO, MJ Fresh Gang, MeeH, XPX, Jendes, Genquo, Suitangtang).

name: Contemporary Sámi dress and design (gákti and duodji revival)
description: Sámi designers of Sápmi (Norway, Sweden) who rework the gákti, horn hat (ládjogahppir), woven belts and silver into everyday clothing: embroidered T-shirts, sweatshirts and caps, reindeer-leather pieces and modern gákti dresses, from Alta and Karasjok labels to Kiruna studios.

name: Colombian swimwear and beachwear (moda baño)
description: Handmade and print-led bikinis, one-pieces and resort pieces from Medellin, Cali, Barranquilla and Bogota labels, shown at Miami Swim Week and Bogota Fashion Week: Agua Bendita, Maaji, OndadeMar, Mola Mola, Palmacea, Waimari, Cala de la Cruz.

name: Yucatecan guayabera
description: The guayabera shirt of Yucatan, celebrated each year in Merida on the Dia de la Guayabera and made by local houses such as Mayakim, Chatre, Guayaberas Dzibichaltun, Euan, Camasha and Dezendo.

name: Paisa urban fashion (Medellin reggaeton streetwear)
description: Medellin streetwear and urban luxury labels tied to the city's reggaeton scene and dressing its artists: Monastery, True, Clemont, Undergold and Nea.
